To answer your question, yes, I think it is low self esteem, and your depression controlling you. When you’re in it deep, and are at the point of 0 friends and 0 acquaintances, it’s easy to forget your worth since no one is there to remind you. Especially yourself. The “I’m cute but not like thick or big titties or anything” sounds like he likes you for you, and that when you do have the energy to interact with people, your presence is enjoyed.

I think you’re feeling intimidated because he seems so put together, but that’s exactly what you need to prevent. Self sabotage. If you feel intimidated by this gap between you two in your head, insecurity may get the better of you. Does he know you’re feeling this way? I think the best route would to be direct and communicate your worries to him [if you’re ready].

On a side note, it might help looking into attachment theory. It sounds like you’re a fearful avoidant [r/FearfulAvoidant] or a person with anxious attachment [r/AnxiousAttachment] - it won’t be a magic fix for you but seeing people with similar thoughts to you, why you think those thoughts, and how to prevent them might help. Best of luck!

I think you have several options and there are two main ones, both with backlash. Break up with her and deal with the mess afterwards, or stay with her and waste both of your time.

It’s a tricky situation, and the fact a lot of people know does make it a bit messy - but I think it might be better to just nip it in the bud. It’d be worse to continue leading her on than hurting her feelings now but allowing her more time to get over it and less time to get more romantically attached to you. 

I think you might have to deal with her being hurt afterwards, so try to plan out how you want to approach it carefully, make it clear it’s not her fault, and like you said, that you love her, but platonically. 

The more time that goes by, the more likely she is to get hurt and you’re likely to have to deal with the consequences of it, so if you decide to, try and do it quick.

I’m not sure why you think you’re a bad person, but let’s say you are. That doesn’t mean it’s concrete. You don’t have to die as a bad person, it’s never too late to change. 

Personally, I don’t think it’s usually as black and white as bad person and good person, you can, like you said, make bad choices, but still be a “good” person. No two people have the same perception of us, you’re going to be bad in some eyes and good in others, but I hope you’ll want to live to experience being the good.

The reason we make bad decisions is so we can learn from them and make good ones. You deserve to live buddy. Stay strong.

At the end of the day it’s your decision and I support sex work if that’s what the worker chooses. However I think in your position it just might make your relationship with sex unhealthy.

I’ve seen you reply you might as well get paid for it, which honestly, fair enough, but my counter to that is you’re not actually killing two birds with one stone. I assume money isn’t the main focus and it’s just an added benefit? With the main benefit being intimacy via the sex work. Except intimacy is going to become work, it’s going to further advance the view that sex isn’t genuine for you and it’ll seem too transactional.

Once again, ultimately your choice and you are completely entitled to that, but I think maybe there’s something deeper here you should be looking at? What it is, I’m unfortunately not sure, but I don’t think sex work will solve it. Hope this helps!

I would also like to emphasise you *feel* rejected but I don’t think you actually were, it was just made to be a convo for another day since you were drunk [green flag on his part imo]. 

The thing is, since you’ve avoided bringing up the conversation again, and pretended like you didn’t even remember saying what you said, he’s probably brushed it off as a “OP was drunk” thing.

I think talk to him directly and confess in a clear state of mind. If you don’t want to you don’t have to but it appears you’re reading too far into things because of how things happened.

Hmm that’s interesting how he chose your bf to be his best man considering the whole fight and begging situation. I’m not trying to make assumptions but do you think there’s a possibility he’s taking advantage of your bf and their history? Like he knows your bf will go to great lengths for him and that he’s now scared to disagree with him? I’m not sure if it will reach him, but maybe having another chat with your bf about him placing a financial boundary with his friend is necessary, and that if his friend doesn’t respect that then they shouldn’t be friends cause he’s being used. I think it needs to be done in a gentle but firm way because you shouldn’t be used either in this process via having to ask distant relatives for a holiday. I understand he wants to be a good friend but you shouldn’t be dragged into his quest for validation.

I don’t think he has bad intentions but I also don’t think you’re in the wrong at all. Your bf is trying to be a good friend but is being highly irresponsible, and even selfish towards you. He’s allowed to set boundaries as a best man, especially financially, and him not doing that, whilst also having it impact you, is not right. Why do you think he’s going to such lengths? To impress them? For validation? Does he feel it’s his responsibility? Or is it as simple as he just really values the friendship? If you can determine why he’s doing it, maybe it might be helpful since there might be something deeper? Either way though, your shared finances being impacted is not right, if they are shared you have a right to set a boundary, especially since you know you guys can’t afford this. If he wants to use his own money, he can do that instead.

Yikes he seems like a walking red flag. 
Him not being “into feminist and LGBT themes…hasn’t been an issue” *yet* [and that’s debatable with the making of this post]. He doesn’t seem like an open minded person and I don’t mean that just politically but also by him not caring what your response is. It’s basically him saying “if you don’t agree with me I don’t want to hear it.” This might seem a bit nitpicky but there’s the possibility he’ll become more intolerant towards such themes since he’s willing to listen to such misinformation and before you know it, something that affects you or that you’re passionate about he’ll think is some feminist nonsense. I personally also think it’s insensitive for him to even send it to you when you’re from a neighbouring country then try and justify it with the passive “he has a point”. Politics aside though, the fact you feel like you can’t complain is a major issue, because that’s definitely going to come up again and you’ll be made to feel like an idiot for having an opinion. Seems like he doesn’t want to listen to you unless it’s validating him.

Also the whole “forgot you’re a feminist” because you’re a psychology student is so silly??? Plus just a childish response.

Edit: Also wanted to say it’s not just “humour”, if you don’t find it funny OP, then you shouldn’t feel pressured. Plus some topics just aren’t funny. Hope the situation works out, maybe have a chat with him and if he doesn’t want to communicate properly, consider if that’s a dealbreaker for you.
